# QS-CFW-9184-50 — Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (4340)
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-9184-50

Scope
This document defines quality acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the crankshaft blank identified as CFW-9184-50, manufactured from steel grade 4340, produced at Plant P3. The intent is to establish mandatory material and dimensional acceptance criteria, outline the inspection methodology to demonstrate conformity, and provide a consistent process for handling nonconforming items. This specification applies to raw forged blanks prior to finish machining and heat treatment operations.

Background and rationale
Crankshaft blanks for high-cycle rotating assemblies require controlled hardness and accurate bore location to ensure final machining yield and finished-component performance. The values stated in this document reflect metallurgical and machining constraints established by design engineering. Inspectors and quality engineers must verify the stated requirements on incoming and in-process forgings to avoid downstream scrap, rework, and latent field failures. The inspection methods described favor traceable, instrumented measurements and documented records to support first article verification and routine production checks.

Requirements table
| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material | 4340 (as specified on part drawing) |
| Hardness range | The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 32-38 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is ±0.02 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 80.8 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and separation defects that would affect machinability or structural integrity (visual and tactile inspection). |
| Traceability | Each forging must be legibly stamped or tagged with the part identifier and a batch or heat number that links to mill certificates. |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspections are performed using calibrated instruments and documented procedures. The emphasis is on objective data capture, clear acceptance criteria, and retention of records that enable traceability to the production batch.

Hardness verification
- Perform hardness testing at locations representative of crank web and journal regions to assess bulk condition prior to finish heat treatment. Use a calibrated portable hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale and following the instrument manufacturer's procedure.
- Record measured values and compare against the requirement: The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 32-38 HRC. Any measured value outside this stated range is a basis for nonconformance.

Bore diameter verification
- Measure the bore diameter using an appropriate bore gauge or inside micrometer capable of the required resolution. Verify measurements at nominal bore locations specified on the engineering drawing.
- Document measured values and verify compliance with the tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is ±0.02 mm. Records must show measured dimension, instrument used, and the inspector's identification.

Weight verification
- Weigh the forging on a calibrated scale capable of handling the part mass. Compare the measured weight to the maximum forging weight requirement: The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 80.8 kg.
- If weight is at or below the stated value, the forging meets the weight requirement; weigh and record per lot.

Surface and defect inspection
- Perform visual inspection under appropriate lighting with supplemental tactile examination. Reject parts exhibiting forging defects that compromise machinability or fatigue integrity, and record defect type and location.

Sampling and acceptance note
- The inspection methods described are intended for first article and routine production verification. When sampling is employed, ensure the sampling plan is documented and justified in the inspection record. The acceptance or rejection of items always references the stated requirements in the requirements table.

Examples and illustrative scenarios
- Example: A forging measured during first article has hardness readings of values within the specified HRC band; record entry shows tester identification and instrument calibration identifier. The item proceeds to the next operation.
- Example: A forging measured for bore diameter shows deviation beyond the stated bore tolerance; the forging is segregated and the nonconformance process is invoked.

Records to keep
- Inspection checklist showing item identifier, part number CFW-9184-50, batch or heat number, measured hardness values, instrument identification, instrument calibration references, measured bore diameters, measured weight, inspector name, and date.
- Nonconformance report for any item failing to meet the requirements in the requirements table, including disposition and corrective action.
- Traceability records linking each forging to its mill certificate and heat lot.
- First article inspection report for initial production lots and any process change affecting material, tooling, or heat treat practice.

Nonconformance handling
Disposition process
- Any forging that does not meet the requirements listed in the requirements table is to be segregated and clearly identified. The nonconforming item must not proceed to downstream operations until disposition is approved by quality engineering and any required corrective actions are completed.
- Nonconformance reports shall include the observed deviation, reference to the applicable requirement (for example, the exact text for hardness, bore tolerance, or maximum weight), the lot identity, and a proposed disposition.

Root cause and corrective action
- Quality engineering will lead or coordinate a root cause evaluation for systemic deviations. Corrective actions may include process adjustments, additional inspection steps, or supplier escalation. Records of the root cause analysis and corrective action implementation are to be retained with the nonconformance file.

Returns to service
- Authorized rework or acceptance by concession must be documented and include verification steps that confirm the forging now meets the stated requirements. Re-inspection records must reference the original nonconformance report.

Related documents
- None

Revision history
- Revision: Rev C (current document control designation).
